text:
lee_sre: Noticing a burst of apiserver 5xxs in us-central1 starting ~10m ago. Symptoms: proxy errors and a growing watch backlog, intermittent 502s.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] apiserver 5xx surge detected (us-central1) - 5m window.

lee_sre: paste from apiserver logs:
```
E0504 09:12:07.221 apiserver.go:290] http: proxy error: dial tcp 10.10.4.3:6443: connect: connection reset by peer
E0504 09:12:07.456 apiserver.go:305] watch queue backlog: 3769
```

mina: digging into infra metrics
 - NAT ephemeral port usage hit 96% during the annex nodepool attach. conntrack_count also spiked on kube-proxy.

oscar: saw a large parallel attach of GPU nodes from the autoscaler at 09:05 (preemptible batch). kubelet heartbeats + image pulls created a lot of outbound connections.

tammy: there was a transient MTU mismatch reported by one edge router earlier at 08:59 but that recovered. maybe contributed to retransmits.

lee_sre: probable chain: parallel attaches -> conntrack/NAT port exhaustion -> apiserver resets and proxy errors -> watch backlog grows -> etcd sees commit latency spikes.

mina: short-term playbook I can run now: 1) enable port-preserving SNAT for the regional NAT, 2) spin up a second NAT gateway as backup, 3) throttle autoscaler concurrency to stagger attaches.

oscar: i'll roll a canary to set max_parallel_attach=4 and attach_backoff_seconds=20. keeping canary to 10% nodepool first.

billing-bot: [INFO] Estimated extra cost for second NAT (regional) = $190/day.

lee_sre: tammy, can you route control-plane egress to the spare NAT for 30m while we validate? mark as emergency change and post once done.

tammy: routing done. monitoring shows apiserver errors dropping within 2m. watch backlog down to ~600.

oscar: canary pushed. will observe for 30m. deploy-bot: gpu-autoscaler v3.2.1-canary scheduled.

lee_sre: follow-ups: add alert for NAT ephemeral > 90% (1m), apiserver watch backlog > 1000 (2m), etcd commit latency > 120ms (1m). INFRA ticket for NAT sizing + autoscaler throttling.

mina: INFRA-8104 created, attaching conntrack dumps and NAT usage graphs.

billing-bot: [ACTION] CM-4191 created to model dedicated vs preemptible GPU split for reliability tradeoff (assign billing & infra).

lee_sre: long-term suggestions: reserve a small warm pool of non-preemptible GPUs for rapid scale, move control-plane egress off shared customer NATs, and add synthetic watch stress to the canary pipeline.

mina: agreed. also recommend making node onboarding quieter: reduce kubelet burst and stagger image pulls via local cache warming.

lee_sre: great work. will reconvene after the canary window. thanks all.
